chose: buildMessages returns [system, fixed user trigger] two-message array
because: ai@7's standardizePrompt throws 'System messages are not allowed in the prompt or messages fields' unless allowSystemInMessages is set, and separately refuses an empty messages array - a request cannot be only a system message, so a fixed non-templated trigger user turn is required structurally

chose: resolveProvider() lazily imports @ai-sdk/openai-compatible inside the moonshot registry entry, is async
because: plan §4 requires run:once and every non-LLM code path to never pull LLM SDKs in eagerly, mirroring how web treats pg; an async factory keyed by LLM_ENRICHMENT_PROVIDER is the only way to keep the import lazy while still returning a LanguageModel

chose: no default baked in for LLM_ENRICHMENT_PROVIDER or LLM_ENRICHMENT_MODEL - both throw a specific actionable error when unset
over: defaulting LLM_ENRICHMENT_PROVIDER to moonshot since it is the only registry entry
because: plan §6.1 explicitly says a wrong hardcoded model id should be a deploy-time error someone reads, not a maintained constant; extending that same reasoning to the provider name keeps exactly one place (env) deciding which provider runs and avoids a silent moonshot default masking a missing env var in a new deploy

chose: classifyWithLlm returns validated LlmOutput plus usage/latency/messages/outputChoices/httpStatus(undefined)/warnings - stops short of DB or merge.ts
over: having classify.ts call merge.ts or write labels directly
because: plan §4 draws the line at 'build messages (pure) -> generateObject -> validate -> map to candidate Labels (pure)' with merge.ts owning the Label mapping; classify.ts must not import merge.ts or capture.ts so steps.ts (another concurrent agent's file) is the only wiring point

chose: no mode:'json' fallback in classifyWithLlm - generateObject called with defaults only
over: implementing a mode:'json' fallback path per plan §7.1's contingent wording
because: installed ai@7.0.79's generateObject signature (node_modules/ai/dist/index.d.ts) has no mode option at all - the plan's own instruction was to decide based on what the installed major actually supports, and it supports nothing there is to fall back to

chose: LlmClassifyResult.httpStatus is always undefined from a successful call today, field kept for shape stability
over: omitting httpStatus from the result entirely
because: ai@7's GenerateObjectResult/LanguageModelResponseMetadata exposes response.headers and .body but no numeric status field on success - there is nothing to populate it from without inventing a header-parsing heuristic that would be provider-specific and untestable against the mock

chose: maxOutputTokens default 4096, sized off the dense worst-case slug count (28 entries) not the sparse common case
over: a smaller default like 1024 sized to the typical sparse response
because: the schema allows up to 28 entries (10 allergens + 13 diets + 2 cuisine + 2 mealType + 1 spiceLevel) each up to ~120 tokens with a 500-char note; truncating a rare everything-flagged recipe mid-JSON would turn a valid dense response into a schema-rejected error the retry-then-error path would treat as Kimi malfunctioning rather than a token budget problem

chose: ai@7.0.79's generateObject is marked @deprecated in its own JSDoc ('Use generateText with an output setting instead') yet is fully typed, exported, and functionally exercised end-to-end against MockLanguageModelV4 with no runtime warning
couldBe: the instrument is wrong — the thing that PRODUCED this number, not the thing it describes

ai@7 kept generateObject as a stable, still-supported convenience wrapper during a slow migration window rather than a function on an imminent removal path; OR the deprecation is real and forward-looking and this plan's L5 pin to generateObject will need a follow-up migration to generateText({output}) before a future ai major removes it
discriminatedBy: checking the ai package's CHANGELOG/release notes for a stated removal version, or watching for a runtime deprecation warning under AI_SDK_LOG_WARNINGS once real (human-run) traffic exercises it

over: add an invariant or boundary claim that the change does not require
because: this slice's behavioral surface (buildRecipeJson, buildMessages, classifyWithLlm, resolveProvider) is orchestration over an already-pinned contract: the closed slug enums and LLM_ENRICHMENT_VERSION are pinned in llm/schema.test.ts (owned by another agent, unmodified here), and this file's own new behavior -- the two-message system+trigger shape, schema-rejection wrapping into LlmClassifyError with rawText, abort propagation -- is exhaustively asserted in classify.test.ts's 13 cases rather than needing a separate anchor; there is no new cross-module invariant this slice introduces beyond what those tests already fence in

chose: deprecation is real and intentional (confirmed by two separate deliberate changelog entries), but generateObject remains a stable, fully-typed, unremoved convenience wrapper with no stated removal version -- the plan's L5 pin to it is safe for now; a future migration to generateText({output}) is warranted before whatever ai major eventually removes it, not urgent today
because: node_modules/ai/CHANGELOG.md shows generateObject/streamObject were deliberately deprecated at 614599a (v6.0.0-beta.127, in favor of 'stable structured output on generateText/streamText/ToolLoopAgent' per 077aea3) and their mode option was separately removed at af9dab3 -- both are real, intentional API-narrowing changes, not JSDoc leftovers. No removal version for generateObject itself appears anywhere in the changelog through the installed v7.0.79, unlike other deprecations in the same file that explicitly say 'will be removed in the next major release' -- so it is confirmed real but not on an announced removal path yet.
